title.zh: 卷四十九 志第二 天文二
title.raw: 卷四十九 志第二 天文二 Volume 49 Treatises 2: Astronomy 2

translations.literal: The Purple Forbidden Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: The Purple Forbidden Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 紫微垣東蕃八星，西蕃七星，在北斗北，左右環列，翊衛之象也。

translations.literal: The Purple Forbidden Enclosure has eight stars in its eastern rampart and seven in its western rampart; north of the Northern Dipper, arrayed left and right in a ring — the image of assisting guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Purple Forbidden Enclosure comprises eight stars in its eastern rampart and seven in its western rampart. Lying north of the Northern Dipper and arrayed in a ring to left and right, it embodies the figure of guardian attendants.

sentences.zh: 一曰大帝之坐，天子之常居也，主命、主度也。

translations.literal: It is also called the Seat of the Great Thearch — the Son of Heaven's constant abode; it governs lifespan and governs the celestial degrees.
translations.idiomatic: It is also called the Seat of the Great Thearch—the Son of Heaven's usual dwelling—and it governs fate and the gradations of the heavens.

sentences.zh: 東蕃近閶闔門第一星爲左樞，第二星爲上宰，三星曰少宰，四星曰上弼一曰上輔，五星爲少弼一曰少輔，六星爲上衛，七星爲少衛，八星爲少丞或曰上丞。

translations.literal: In the eastern rampart nearest to the Gate of Heaven: the first star is the Left Pivot; the second is the Supreme Steward; the third is called the Lesser Steward; the fourth is called the Supreme Assistant, also called the Supreme Aide; the fifth is the Lesser Assistant, also called the Lesser Aide; the sixth is the Supreme Guard; the seventh is the Lesser Guard; the eighth is the Lesser Chancellor, or called the Supreme Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern rampart nearest to the Gate of Heaven: the first star is the Left Pivot; the second, the Supreme Steward; the third, the Lesser Steward; the fourth, the Supreme Assistant (also called the Supreme Aide); the fifth, the Lesser Assistant (also called the Lesser Aide); the sixth, the Supreme Guard; the seventh, the Lesser Guard; and the eighth, the Lesser Chancellor—also called the Supreme Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 其西蕃近閶闔門第一星爲右樞，第二星爲少尉，第三星爲上輔，第四星爲少輔，第五星爲上衛，第六星爲少衛，第七星爲上丞。

translations.literal: In its western rampart nearest to the Gate of Heaven: the first star is the Right Pivot; the second is the Lesser Commandant; the third is the Supreme Aide; the fourth is the Lesser Aide; the fifth is the Supreme Guard; the sixth is the Lesser Guard; the seventh is the Supreme Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the western rampart nearest to the Gate of Heaven: the first star is the Right Pivot; the second, the Lesser Commandant; the third, the Supreme Aide; the fourth, the Lesser Aide; the fifth, the Supreme Guard; the sixth, the Lesser Guard; and the seventh, the Supreme Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 其占，欲均明，大小有常，則內輔盛；

translations.literal: In its prognostication, one desires them evenly bright, with size constant — then the inner aides flourish;
translations.idiomatic: In prognostication, when the stars are evenly bright and their sizes remain constant, the inner aides prosper;

translations.literal: when the enclosure wall is straight, the Son of Heaven personally leads troops on campaign;
translations.idiomatic: when the enclosure wall stands straight, the Son of Heaven will personally lead an expedition;

translations.literal: when the gate opens, armies rise at the palace walls.
translations.idiomatic: when the gate opens wide, war arises at the palace walls.

sentences.zh: 兩蕃正南開如門，曰閶闔。

translations.literal: The two ramparts open toward due south like a gate — this is called the Gate of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Where the two ramparts open toward due south like a gate is called the Gate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 有流星自門出四野者，當有中使御命，視其所往分野論之；

translations.literal: When a meteor emerges from the gate into the four quarters, there should be an imperial envoy bearing commands; interpret it according to the territorial division toward which it goes;
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor issues from the gate into the four quarters, an imperial envoy bearing commands is at hand; interpret the omen according to the territorial division toward which it travels;

sentences.zh: 不依門出入者，外蕃國使也。

translations.literal: those that do not enter or exit by the gate are envoys from outer border states.
translations.idiomatic: those that do not pass through the gate are envoys from foreign border states.

sentences.zh: 太陰、歲星犯紫微垣，有喪。

translations.literal: When the Moon or the Year Star encroaches upon the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, there is mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Moon or the Year Star transgresses the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, mourning follows.

translations.literal: When the Great White or the Chronogram Star encroaches upon it, the age changes.
translations.idiomatic: When Venus or Mercury transgresses it, the age turns over.

translations.literal: When the Sparkling Deluder stations itself in the palace, the ruler loses his position.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars stations itself in the palace, the ruler loses his throne.

translations.literal: When a guest star stations itself there, there is a disloyal minister and the state changes its government.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star stations itself there, a disloyal minister arises and the state changes its regime.

translations.literal: The State Sovereign star — war.
translations.idiomatic: The State Sovereign star presages war.

translations.literal: When a comet encroaches, a strange king is established.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet transgresses, a usurper king rises.

sentences.zh: 流星犯之，爲兵、喪，水旱不調。

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches upon it, there is war and mourning, and flood and drought fall out of balance.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses it, war and mourning follow, and floods and droughts fall out of balance.

sentences.zh: 使星入北方，兵起石氏云：東西兩蕃總十六星，西蕃亦八星，一右樞，二上尉，三少尉，四上輔，五少輔，六上衛，七少衛，八少丞。

translations.literal: When the envoy star enters the north, armies rise. Master Shi says: the eastern and western ramparts total sixteen stars; the western rampart also has eight stars — first the Right Pivot, second the Supreme Commandant, third the Lesser Commandant, fourth the Supreme Aide, fifth the Lesser Aide, sixth the Supreme Guard, seventh the Lesser Guard, eighth the Lesser Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy star enters the north, war arises. Master Shi says that the eastern and western ramparts together comprise sixteen stars; the western rampart likewise has eight—the Right Pivot, the Supreme Commandant, the Lesser Commandant, the Supreme Aide, the Lesser Aide, the Supreme Guard, the Lesser Guard, and the Lesser Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 上宰一星，上輔二星，三公也。

translations.literal: The Supreme Steward is one star; the Supreme Aides are two stars — the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Steward is a single star; the Supreme Aides are two stars—the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 少宰一星，少輔二星，三孤也。

translations.literal: The Lesser Steward is one star; the Lesser Aides are two stars — the Three Solitaries.
translations.idiomatic: The Lesser Steward is a single star; the Lesser Aides are two stars—the Three Solitaries.

translations.literal: These are the Three Excellencies and Three Solitaries at court.
translations.idiomatic: These represent the Three Excellencies and Three Solitaries at court.

sentences.zh: 左右樞、上少丞，疑丞輔弼，四鄰之謂也。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Pivots, the Supreme and Lesser Chancellors — presumably chancellors, aides, and assistants; this is what is meant by the four neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Pivots and the Supreme and Lesser Chancellors—presumably chancellors, aides, and assistants—are what is meant by the four neighbors.

sentences.zh: 尉二星，衛四星，六軍大副尉，四衛將軍也。

translations.literal: The Commandants are two stars; the Guards are four stars — the great deputy commandants of the Six Armies, the four guard generals.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandants are two stars and the Guards four—the great deputy commandants of the Six Armies and the four guard generals.

sentences.zh: 北極五星，在紫微宮中，北辰最尊者也，其紐星爲天樞，天運無窮，三光迭耀，而極星不移，故曰「居其所而衆星共之」。

translations.literal: The Five Stars of the North Pole are within the Purple Forbidden Palace; the North Star is the most honored. Its pivot star is the Celestial Pivot. The heavenly revolutions are endless; the three luminaries shine in succession, yet the pole star does not move — hence it is said, 'Remaining in its place, the myriad stars revolve about it.'
translations.idiomatic: The Five Stars of the North Pole lie within the Purple Forbidden Palace; the North Star is the most exalted. Its pivot star is the Celestial Pivot. Though the heavens turn without end and the three luminaries shine in turn, the pole star does not stir—hence the saying, 'Remaining in its place, the myriad stars revolve about it.'

sentences.zh: 樞星在天心，四方去極各九十一度。

translations.literal: The Pivot star is at the heart of heaven; the four quarters are each ninety-one degrees from the pole.
translations.idiomatic: The Pivot star stands at the heart of heaven; from the pole each of the four quarters lies ninety-one degrees distant.

sentences.zh: 賈逵、張衡、蔡邕、王蕃、陸績皆以北極紐星之樞，是不動處。

translations.literal: Jia Kui, Zhang Heng, Cai Yong, Wang Fan, and Lu Ji all held that the pivot of the North Pole's pivot star is the unmoving point.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kui, Zhang Heng, Cai Yong, Wang Fan, and Lu Ji all identified the pivot of the North Pole's pivot star as the unmoving point.

translations.literal: It lies at the end of the pivot star, still more than one degree beyond.
translations.idiomatic: It lies at the tip of the pivot star, still more than one degree beyond.

translations.literal: At the present Clear Terrace it is four and a half degrees from the pole.
translations.idiomatic: At the present Clear Terrace observatory it stands four and a half degrees from the pole.

translations.literal: the first star governs the moon — the Heir Apparent;
translations.idiomatic: The first star governs the moon—the Heir Apparent;

sentences.zh: 二星主日，帝王也，亦太一之坐，謂最赤明者也；

translations.literal: the second star governs the sun — the emperor; it is also the Seat of the Great Unity, called the most red and bright;
translations.idiomatic: the second star governs the sun—the emperor; it is also the Seat of the Great Unity, the most red and brilliant of them;

translations.literal: the third star governs the Five Phases — the secondary sons.
translations.idiomatic: the third star governs the Five Phases—the secondary sons.

sentences.zh: 《乾象新星書》曰：「第三星主五行，第四星主諸王，第五星爲後宮。

translations.literal: The New Star Book of the Qianxiang says: 'The third star governs the Five Phases; the fourth star governs the various kings; the fifth star is the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: The New Star Book of the Qianxiang says: 'The third star governs the Five Phases; the fourth governs the various princes; the fifth is the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 」閎云：「北極五星，初一曰帝，次二曰後，次三曰妃，次四曰太子，次五曰庶子。

translations.literal: ' Hong says: 'Of the Five Stars of the North Pole, the first is called the Emperor; the second, the Empress; the third, the Consort; the fourth, the Heir Apparent; the fifth, the secondary son.
translations.idiomatic: ' Hong says: 'Of the Five Stars of the North Pole, the first is the Emperor; the second, the Empress; the third, the Consort; the fourth, the Heir Apparent; the fifth, the secondary son.

translations.literal: ' The fourth, called the Heir Apparent, is the most red and bright.
translations.idiomatic: ' The fourth, called the Heir Apparent, is the most red and brilliant.

sentences.zh: 後四星勾曲以抱之者，帝星也。

translations.literal: The four stars behind curve and embrace it — this is the Emperor star.
translations.idiomatic: The four stars behind curve inward to embrace it—this is the Emperor star.

sentences.zh: 太公望以爲北辰，以爲耀魄寶，以爲帝極者是也。

translations.literal: Taigong Wang held that the North Star, the Radiant Soul Treasure, and the Imperial Pole are this.
translations.idiomatic: Taigong Wang identified the North Star, the Radiant Soul Treasure, and the Imperial Pole with this star.

sentences.zh: 或以勾陳口中一星爲耀魄寶者，非是。

translations.literal: Some take the single star in the mouth of the Hook Array to be the Radiant Soul Treasure — this is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Some identify the single star in the mouth of the Hook Array as the Radiant Soul Treasure—this is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 北極中星不明，主不用事；

translations.literal: when the central star of the North Pole is not bright, the ruler does not attend to affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When the central star of the North Pole is dim, the ruler neglects his duties;

translations.literal: when the right star is not bright, the Heir Apparent is troubled;
translations.idiomatic: when the right star is dim, the Heir Apparent is in distress;

translations.literal: when the left star is not bright, the secondary sons are troubled;
translations.idiomatic: when the left star is dim, the secondary sons are in distress;

translations.literal: when bright and large and trembling, the ruler loves to go on excursions;
translations.idiomatic: when it shines large and trembles, the ruler is fond of travel;

translations.literal: when the color is bluish and faint, it is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: when its color turns bluish and faint, the omen is dire.

translations.literal: When a guest star enters, there is war and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star enters, war and mourning follow.

translations.literal: When a comet enters, there is a change of position.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet enters, the throne changes hands.

translations.literal: When a meteor enters, armies rise and the earth quakes.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor enters, war arises and the earth trembles.

sentences.zh: 北斗七星在太微北，杓攜龍角，衡殷南斗，魁枕參首，是爲帝車，運於中央，臨制四海，以建四時、均五行、移節度、定諸紀，乃七政之樞機，陰陽之元本也。

translations.literal: The Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper are north of the Supreme Palace Enclosure; the ladle carries the Dragon's Horn, the Balance presses upon the Southern Dipper, the Chief rests upon the head of Shen — this is the Emperor's chariot, revolving at the center, overseeing and governing the four seas, establishing the four seasons, balancing the Five Phases, shifting the nodes and degrees, and fixing the various reckonings. It is the pivot of the Seven Regulators and the primal root of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: The Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper lie north of the Supreme Palace Enclosure: the ladle reaches toward the Dragon's Horn, the Balance presses upon the Southern Dipper, and the Chief rests upon the head of Shen. This is the Emperor's chariot, turning at the center to govern the four seas—establishing the four seasons, balancing the Five Phases, shifting the nodes and degrees, and fixing the celestial reckonings. It is the pivot of the Seven Regulators and the primal root of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 魁第一星曰天樞，正星，主天。

translations.literal: The first star of the Chief is called the Celestial Pivot — the principal star, governing Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The first star of the Chief is called the Celestial Pivot—the principal star, governing Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又曰樞爲天，主陽德，天子象。

translations.literal: It is also said that the Pivot is Heaven, governing yang virtue — the image of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It is also said that the Pivot is Heaven, governing yang virtue—the image of the Son of Heaven.

translations.literal: Its territorial division is Qin; the Han Treatise governs Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its territorial division is Qin; the Han Treatise assigns it to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 《天象占》曰：「天子不恭宗廟，不敬鬼神，則不明，變色。

translations.literal: The Prognostication of Celestial Appearances says: 'If the Son of Heaven is not reverent toward the ancestral temple and does not respect ghosts and spirits, then it is not bright and changes color.
translations.idiomatic: The Prognostication of Celestial Appearances says: 'If the Son of Heaven is not reverent toward the ancestral temple and does not honor ghosts and spirits, the star grows dim and changes color.

translations.literal: ' The second is called Xuan — the law star, governing Earth.
translations.idiomatic: ' The second is called Xuan—the law star, governing Earth.

sentences.zh: 又曰璿爲地，主陰刑，女主象。

translations.literal: It is also said that Xuan is Earth, governing yin punishment — the image of the chief consort.
translations.idiomatic: It is also said that Xuan is Earth, governing yin punishment—the image of the chief consort.

translations.literal: Its territorial division is Chu; the Han Treatise governs Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its territorial division is Chu; the Han Treatise assigns it to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 《天象占》曰：「若廣營宮室，妄鑿山陵，則不明，變色。

translations.literal: The Prognostication of Celestial Appearances says: 'If one broadly constructs palaces and recklessly excavates mountain tombs, then it is not bright and changes color.
translations.idiomatic: The Prognostication of Celestial Appearances says: 'If one extravagantly builds palaces and recklessly excavates mountain tombs, the star grows dim and changes color.

sentences.zh: 」三曰璣，爲人，主火，爲令星，主中禍。

translations.literal: ' The third is called Ji — governing humanity, governing fire; it is the command star, governing mid-level calamities.
translations.idiomatic: ' The third is called Ji—it governs humanity and fire; it is the command star and presides over mid-level calamities.

translations.literal: Its territorial division is Liang; the Han Treatise governs Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its territorial division is Liang; the Han Treatise assigns it to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 若王者不恤民，驟征役，則不明，變色。

translations.literal: If the king does not care for the people and suddenly levies corvée labor, then it is not bright and changes color.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler neglects the people and suddenly imposes corvée labor, the star grows dim and changes color.

sentences.zh: 四曰權，爲時，主水，爲伐星，主天理，伐無道。

translations.literal: The fourth is called Quan — governing the seasons, governing water; it is the punitive star, governing heavenly principle, punishing the wayless.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth is called Quan—it governs the seasons and water; it is the punitive star, upholding heavenly principle and punishing the wayless.

translations.literal: Its territorial division is Wu; the Han Treatise governs Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its territorial division is Wu; the Han Treatise assigns it to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 若號令不順四時，則不明，變色。

translations.literal: If commands and edicts do not accord with the four seasons, then it is not bright and changes color.
translations.idiomatic: If commands and edicts fail to accord with the four seasons, the star grows dim and changes color.

sentences.zh: 五曰玉衡，爲音，主土，爲殺星，主中央，助四方，殺有罪。

translations.literal: The fifth is called the Jade Scepter — governing sound, governing earth; it is the killing star, governing the center, assisting the four quarters, executing the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth is called the Jade Scepter—it governs sound and earth; it is the killing star, presiding over the center, assisting the four quarters, and executing the guilty.

translations.literal: Its territorial division is Yan; the Han Treatise governs Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its territorial division is Yan; the Han Treatise assigns it to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 若廢正樂，務淫聲，則不明，變色。

translations.literal: If one abandons orthodox music and pursues licentious sounds, then it is not bright and changes color.
translations.idiomatic: If one abandons orthodox music and pursues licentious sounds, the star grows dim and changes color.

sentences.zh: 六曰闓陽，爲律，主木，爲危星，主天倉、五穀。

translations.literal: The sixth is called Kaiyang — governing pitch pipes, governing wood; it is the peril star, governing the Heavenly Granary and the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth is called Kaiyang—it governs pitch pipes and wood; it is the peril star, presiding over the Heavenly Granary and the five grains.

translations.literal: Its territorial division is Zhao; the Han Treatise governs Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its territorial division is Zhao; the Han Treatise assigns it to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 若不勸農桑，峻刑法，退賢能，則不明，變色。

translations.literal: If one does not encourage agriculture and sericulture, makes punishments harsh, and dismisses the worthy and capable, then it is not bright and changes color.
translations.idiomatic: If one fails to encourage agriculture and sericulture, makes punishments harsh, and dismisses the worthy and capable, the star grows dim and changes color.

sentences.zh: 七曰搖光，爲星，主金，爲部星，爲應星，主兵。

translations.literal: The seventh is called Yaoguang — governing stars, governing metal; it is the division star, the responding star, governing warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh is called Yaoguang—it governs stars and metal; it is the division star and the responding star, presiding over warfare.

translations.literal: Its territorial division is Qi; the Han Treatise governs Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Its territorial division is Qi; the Han Treatise assigns it to Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 王者聚金寶，不修德，則不明，變色。

translations.literal: If the king amasses gold and treasures but does not cultivate virtue, then it is not bright and changes color.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler hoards gold and treasures but neglects virtue, the star grows dim and changes color.

sentences.zh: 又曰一至四爲魁，魁爲璿璣；

translations.literal: It is also said that the first through fourth form the Chief; the Chief is Xuan and Ji;
translations.idiomatic: It is also said that stars one through four form the Chief; the Chief comprises Xuan and Ji;

sentences.zh: 五至七爲杓，杓爲玉衡：是爲七政，星明其國昌。

translations.literal: the fifth through seventh form the Ladle; the Ladle is the Jade Scepter — these are the Seven Regulators; when the stars are bright, that state flourishes.
translations.idiomatic: stars five through seven form the Ladle; the Ladle is the Jade Scepter—these are the Seven Regulators; when the stars shine bright, the state prospers.

sentences.zh: 第八曰弼星，在第七星右，不見，《漢志》主幽州。

translations.literal: The eighth is called the Assisting Star, to the right of the seventh star, invisible; the Han Treatise governs Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The eighth is called the Assisting Star, to the right of the seventh star and invisible; the Han Treatise assigns it to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 第九曰輔星，在第六星左，常見，《漢志》主并州。

translations.literal: The ninth is called the Aide Star, to the left of the sixth star, always visible; the Han Treatise governs Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth is called the Aide Star, to the left of the sixth star and always visible; the Han Treatise assigns it to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 《晉志》，輔星傅乎闓陽，所以佐鬥成功，丞相之象也。

translations.literal: The Jin Treatise: the Aide Star adjoins Kaiyang — thereby assisting the Dipper in achieving success; it is the image of the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Treatise states that the Aide Star adjoins Kaiyang, thereby assisting the Dipper in its work—the image of the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 其色在春青黃，在夏赤黃，秋爲白黃，冬爲黑黃。

translations.literal: Its color in spring is bluish-yellow; in summer, red-yellow; in autumn, white-yellow; in winter, black-yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Its color in spring is bluish-yellow; in summer, red-yellow; in autumn, white-yellow; in winter, black-yellow.

sentences.zh: 變常則國有兵殃，明則臣強。

translations.literal: When it changes from the norm, the state suffers military calamity; when bright, ministers are strong.
translations.idiomatic: When it changes from its normal appearance, the state suffers military disaster; when bright, ministers grow powerful.

sentences.zh: 鬥旁欲多星則安，鬥中星少則人恐。

translations.literal: One desires many stars beside the Dipper for peace; few stars within the Dipper and the people are fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Many stars beside the Dipper betoken peace; few stars within the Dipper and the people live in fear.

translations.literal: When the Moon encroaches upon it, there is war, mourning, and a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When the Moon transgresses it, war, mourning, and a great amnesty follow.

translations.literal: A white halo piercing three stars — the king regards it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: A white halo piercing three stars is an ill omen for the king.

translations.literal: When a broom star appears at the Northern Dipper, it governs peril.
translations.idiomatic: When a broom star appears at the Northern Dipper, peril is at hand.

translations.literal: When a comet encroaches, the ruler is changed.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet transgresses, the ruler is replaced.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses:

translations.literal: there is warfare between host and guest.
translations.idiomatic: host and guest armies clash.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches, there is war.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses, war follows.

translations.literal: When the Five Stars encroach upon it, the state is in disorder and the ruler is changed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Planets transgress it, the state falls into disorder and the ruler is replaced.

sentences.zh: 按：北斗與輔星爲八，而《漢志》云九星，武密及楊維德皆採用之。

translations.literal: Note: the Northern Dipper with the Aide Star makes eight, yet the Han Treatise speaks of nine stars; Wu Mi and Yang Weide both adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: Note: the Northern Dipper together with the Aide Star makes eight, yet the Han Treatise speaks of nine stars; Wu Mi and Yang Weide both adopted this reckoning.

sentences.zh: 《史記索隱》云：「北斗星間相去各九千里。

translations.literal: The Shiji Hidden Glosses says: 'Between the stars of the Northern Dipper the distance is nine thousand li each.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiji Hidden Glosses says: 'Between the stars of the Northern Dipper the distance is nine thousand li each.

sentences.zh: 其二陰星不見者，相去八千里。

translations.literal: Of its two yin stars that are not visible, the distance between them is eight thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Of its two yin stars that are not visible, the distance between them is eight thousand li.

sentences.zh: 」而丹元子《步天歌》亦云九星，《漢書》必有所本矣。

translations.literal: ' Yet Master Danyuan's Song of Pacing the Heavens also speaks of nine stars — the Book of Han must have had some source for this.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yet Master Danyuan's Song of Pacing the Heavens also speaks of nine stars—the Book of Han must have had authority for this.

sentences.zh: 勾陳六星，在紫宮中，五帝之後宮也，太帝之正妃也，大帝之帝居也。

translations.literal: The six stars of the Hook Array are within the Purple Palace — the rear palace of the Five Thearchs, the principal consort of the Great Thearch, the imperial dwelling of the Great Thearch.
translations.idiomatic: The six stars of the Hook Array lie within the Purple Palace—the rear palace of the Five Thearchs, the principal consort of the Great Thearch, and the imperial dwelling of the Great Thearch.

translations.literal: The Music Apocrypha says: 'It governs the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Music Apocrypha says: 'It governs the rear palace.

translations.literal: ' Wu Xian says: 'It governs the Son of Heaven's guard army.
translations.idiomatic: ' Wu Xian says: 'It governs the Son of Heaven's guard army.

translations.literal: ' The Jingzhou Prognostication: 'It governs the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Jingzhou Prognostication: 'It governs the Grand Marshal.

translations.literal: ' Some say it governs the generals of the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: ' Some say it governs the generals of the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 或曰主三公、三師，爲萬物之母。

translations.literal: Some say it governs the Three Excellencies and Three Preceptors — the mother of the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Some say it governs the Three Excellencies and Three Preceptors—the mother of the myriad things.

sentences.zh: 六星比陳，象六宮之化，其端大星曰元始，餘星乘之曰庶妾，在北極配六輔甘氏曰：勾陳在辰極左，是爲鉤陳衛六軍將軍。

translations.literal: The six stars are arrayed in formation, imaging the transformations of the six palaces; the great star at the head is called the Primal Beginning, and the remaining stars riding upon it are called the secondary consorts, paired with the Six Aides at the North Pole. Master Gan says: the Hook Array is to the left of the celestial pole at Chen — this is the Hook Array guarding the generals of the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: The six stars are arrayed in formation, imaging the transformations of the six palaces. The great star at the head is called the Primal Beginning; the remaining stars attendant upon it are called the secondary consorts, paired with the Six Aides at the North Pole. Master Gan says that the Hook Array lies to the left of the celestial pole at Chen—this is the Hook Array guarding the generals of the Six Armies.

translations.literal: Some take it to be the rear palace — this is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Some identify it with the rear palace—this is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 勾陳口中一星爲陽德，天皇大帝內坐。

translations.literal: The single star in the mouth of the Hook Array is Yang Virtue — the inner seat of the Celestial Thearch.
translations.idiomatic: The single star in the mouth of the Hook Array is Yang Virtue—the inner seat of the Celestial Thearch.

sentences.zh: 或即以爲天皇大帝，非是。

translations.literal: Some directly take it to be the Celestial Thearch — this is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: Some directly identify it with the Celestial Thearch—this is incorrect.

sentences.zh: 其占，色不欲甚明，明即女主惡之。

translations.literal: In its prognostication, one does not desire the color to be too bright; if bright, the chief consort regards it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: In prognostication, the color should not shine too brightly; if it does, the chief consort takes it as a bad omen.

translations.literal: When the star flourishes, the aides are strong;
translations.idiomatic: When the star flourishes, the aides grow powerful;

sentences.zh: 主不用諫，佞人在側，則不見。

translations.literal: If the ruler does not employ remonstrance and flatterers are at his side, it is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign ignores counsel and sycophants crowd his side, the star vanishes from sight.

sentences.zh: 客星入之，色蒼白，將有憂；

translations.literal: When a guest star enters it, pale in color, there will be worry;
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star enters it, wan and ashen, trouble is at hand;

translations.literal: White means establishing generals;
translations.idiomatic: A white hue signifies the elevation of new generals;

translations.literal: Red-black means generals will die.
translations.idiomatic: Red streaked with black portends the death of generals.

translations.literal: When a guest star emerges and its color is red, battles achieve merit;
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star emerges red, warfare wins success;

translations.literal: If it stations itself there, in the rear palace a female attendant seeks to plot.
translations.idiomatic: If it stations itself there, a woman of the inner palace plots treason.

sentences.zh: 彗星犯之，後宮有謀，近臣憂。

translations.literal: When a comet encroaches upon it, the rear palace has plots and close ministers are troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet transgresses it, conspiracy stirs in the inner palace and close ministers are anxious.

translations.literal: When a meteor enters, it means pressing upon the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor enters, the ruler is pressed upon.

translations.literal: When green vapor enters, the great general is troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When green vapor enters, the commander-in-chief is in distress.

sentences.zh: 天皇大帝一星，在勾陳口中，其神曰耀魄寶，主御群靈，執萬神圖，大人之象也。

translations.literal: The Celestial Thearch Great Emperor: one star, in the mouth of the Hook Array; its spirit is called the Radiant Soul Treasure; it governs all numina, holds the chart of ten thousand gods — the image of the great man.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Thearch Great Emperor is a single star set in the mouth of the Hook Array. Its numen is called the Radiant Soul Treasure; it commands the host of spirits and bears the register of ten thousand gods—the celestial image of the supreme ruler.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon it, it means removing the old and spreading the new.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses it, the old is swept away and the new established.

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches upon it, great ministers rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses it, high ministers rebel.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches upon it, the state has worry.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses it, the state faces calamity.

translations.literal: When cloud vapor enters it, moist and lustrous — auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When cloud vapor enters it, rich and glistening, the omen is auspicious.

sentences.zh: 黃白氣入，連大帝坐，臣獻美女；

translations.literal: When yellow-white vapor enters, connecting with the Great Emperor's seat, ministers present beautiful women;
translations.idiomatic: When yellow-white vapor enters and links to the Great Emperor's throne, ministers present beauties to the court;

translations.literal: Emerging above the Celestial Thearch means changing and establishing kings.
translations.idiomatic: Emerging above the Celestial Thearch portends deposing one king and raising another.

sentences.zh: 四輔四星，又名四弼，在極星側，是曰帝之四鄰，所以輔佐北極，而出度授政也。

translations.literal: The Four Assistants: four stars, also called the Four Supports, beside the pole star — they are called the emperor's four neighbors, to assist the North Pole and bestow governance through degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Assistants are four stars, also called the Four Supports, flanking the pole star. Called the emperor's four neighbors, they aid the Celestial Pivot and hand down governance through the degrees of heaven.

translations.literal: Each is four degrees from the pole star.
translations.idiomatic: Each lies four degrees from the pole star.

translations.literal: Hong says: 'The Four Assistants are also called the Central Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Hong says: 'The Four Assistants are also called the Central Dipper.

translations.literal: ' Some take them to be the rear palace — this is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: ' Some identify them with the inner palace—this is incorrect.

translations.literal: Wu Mi says: 'When the light floats and shifts, it is inauspicious;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mi says: 'When their light wavers and shifts, disaster follows;

translations.literal: small yet bright is auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: a small yet steady brilliance brings good fortune;

translations.literal: dim — then no governance.
translations.idiomatic: dimness signifies disorder in government.'

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon them, great ministers are troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses them, high ministers are in distress.

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches upon them, powerful ministers die.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses them, powerful ministers die.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches upon them, great ministers are dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses them, high ministers are dismissed.

translations.literal: When yellow and white vapor enters, the Four Assistants have joy.
translations.idiomatic: When yellow or white vapor enters, the Four Assistants receive good fortune.

translations.literal: When white vapor enters, the chancellor loses position.
translations.idiomatic: When white vapor enters, the chancellor falls from office.

sentences.zh: 五帝內坐五星，在華蓋下，設敘順，帝所居也。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors Inner Seat: five stars, under the Canopy, arranged in order — the emperor's dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors Inner Seat comprises five stars beneath the Canopy, set in proper sequence—the emperor's celestial dwelling.

translations.literal: Color correct — auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: When their color holds true, fortune follows;

translations.literal: color changes — becomes disaster.
translations.idiomatic: when their color shifts, calamity ensues.

sentences.zh: 客星犯紫宮中坐，占爲大臣犯主。

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon the Purple Palace inner seat, the divination is that a great minister encroaches upon the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses the inner seat of the Purple Palace, it is read as a minister overstepping his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 彗、孛犯之，民饑，大臣憂，三年有兵起。

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches upon it, the people hunger, great ministers are troubled; war rises within three years.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses it, famine follows, ministers are anxious, and war arises within three years.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches upon it, war rises and ministers rebel;
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses it, war arises and ministers rebel;

translations.literal: emerging — there will be executions.
translations.idiomatic: its emergence portends executions.

sentences.zh: 雲氣入，色黃，太子即位，期六十日，赤黃，人君有異。

translations.literal: When cloud vapor enters, color yellow — the crown prince ascends the throne, term sixty days; red-yellow — the ruler has an anomaly.
translations.idiomatic: When cloud vapor enters in yellow, the crown prince will ascend within sixty days; red-yellow heralds irregularity in the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 六甲六星，在華蓋杠旁，主分陰陽，配節候，故在帝旁，所以布政教、授農時也。

translations.literal: The Six Jia: six stars, beside the Canopy crossbeam; they govern dividing yin and yang, matching seasonal periods; therefore beside the emperor, to spread governance and teaching and grant agricultural seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Jia are six stars beside the Canopy's crossbeam. They govern the balance of yin and yang and mark the seasonal divisions; stationed near the emperor, they disseminate law and set the times for planting and harvest.

translations.literal: Bright — then yin and yang harmonize;
translations.idiomatic: When bright, yin and yang fall into harmony;

translations.literal: not bright — then cold and heat change seasons;
translations.idiomatic: when dim, cold and warmth exchange seasons out of turn;

translations.literal: star lost — flood and drought untimely.
translations.idiomatic: when the stars vanish, floods and droughts come at the wrong times.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon them, color red — drought;
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses them in red, drought follows;

translations.literal: black — flood;
translations.idiomatic: in black, floods;

translations.literal: white — then many people have plague.
translations.idiomatic: in white, pestilence spreads among the people.

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches upon them, the chief consort issues government orders.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses them, the chief consort issues edicts and governs.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches upon them, flood and drought; ritual specialists executed.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses them, flood or drought follows and diviners are executed.

translations.literal: When cloud vapor encroaches upon them, color yellow — ritual specialists rise.
translations.idiomatic: When yellow cloud vapor transgresses them, diviners rise to prominence.

translations.literal: Pale — historiographers receive noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Pale vapor means historiographers receive ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 柱史一星，在北極東，主記過，左右史之象。

translations.literal: The Pillar Scribe: one star, east of the North Pole; it governs recording faults — the image of the Left and Right Scribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Pillar Scribe is a single star east of the North Pole. It governs the recording of transgressions and represents the Left and Right Scribes.

sentences.zh: 一云在天柱前，司上帝之言動。

translations.literal: One account places it before the Heavenly Pillar, overseeing the Celestial Lord's words and actions.
translations.idiomatic: Another tradition places it before the Heavenly Pillar, overseeing the Celestial Lord's speech and conduct.

translations.literal: Star bright — historiographers obtain worthy men;
translations.idiomatic: When the star shines bright, worthy men fill the historiographical offices;

translations.literal: not bright — the opposite.
translations.idiomatic: when dim, the reverse holds.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon it, historiographers are dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses it, scribes are dismissed.

sentences.zh: 彗、孛犯，太子憂，或百官黜。

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches upon it, the crown prince is troubled, or the hundred officials are dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses it, the crown prince is in distress, or officials throughout the bureaucracy are dismissed.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches upon it, the ruler has blame.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses it, fault falls upon the sovereign.

translations.literal: When cloud vapor encroaches upon it, color yellow — the scribes have noble rank and salary.
translations.idiomatic: When yellow cloud vapor transgresses it, scribes receive ennoblement and stipends.

translations.literal: When pale vapor enters, the Left and Right Scribes die.
translations.idiomatic: When pale vapor enters, the Left and Right Scribes die.

sentences.zh: 女史一星，在柱史北，婦人之微者，主傳漏。

translations.literal: The Female Scribe: one star, north of the Pillar Scribe; minor women, governs transmitting the clepsydra.
translations.idiomatic: The Female Scribe is a single star north of the Pillar Scribe—a minor feminine presence governing the relay of the water clock.

sentences.zh: 天柱五星，在東垣下，一云在五帝左稍前，主建政教。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Pillar: five stars, under the eastern rampart; one account places them slightly before the Five Emperors on the left; they govern establishing governance and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Pillar comprises five stars beneath the eastern rampart. One tradition places them just ahead of the Five Emperors to the left; they govern the founding of law and learning.

sentences.zh: 一曰法五行，主晦朔、晝夜之職。

translations.literal: Also called governing the Five Phases; they govern duties of new and full moon, day and night.
translations.idiomatic: They are also said to embody the Five Phases and oversee calendrical duties of new moon, full moon, day, and night.

translations.literal: Bright and correct — then auspicious, people secure, yin and yang harmonized;
translations.idiomatic: When bright and steady, fortune follows—the people are at peace and yin and yang are in balance;

translations.literal: otherwise — the calendar officers err.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the calendar officers fall into error.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon them, there are thieves in the state.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses them, bandits arise within the realm.

sentences.zh: 彗、孛犯，宗廟不安，君憂，一曰三公當之。

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches upon them, the ancestral temple is unsettled, the ruler troubled; one account says the Three Excellencies bear it.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses them, the ancestral temple is unsettled and the sovereign is troubled—or, by one account, the Three Excellencies bear the calamity.

translations.literal: Cloud vapor red-yellow — the ruler rejoices;
translations.idiomatic: Red-yellow cloud vapor brings joy to the ruler;

translations.literal: black — the Three Excellencies die.
translations.idiomatic: black portends the death of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 女御四星，在大帝北，一云在勾陳腹，一云在帝坐東北，御妻之象也。

translations.literal: The Female Attendants: four stars, north of the Great Emperor; one account places them in the belly of the Hook Array; one account northeast of the Emperor's Seat — the image of imperial consorts.
translations.idiomatic: The Female Attendants are four stars north of the Great Emperor. One tradition sets them in the belly of the Hook Array; another, northeast of the Emperor's Seat—they represent the sovereign's consorts.

translations.literal: Star bright — many favored within.
translations.idiomatic: When the stars shine bright, the inner palace teems with favored consorts.

sentences.zh: 客星犯之，後宮有誅，一云自戮。

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon them, the rear palace has executions; one account says self-slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses them, bloodshed follows in the inner palace—or, by one account, suicide.

translations.literal: When a broom star or comet encroaches upon them, the rear palace has executions.
translations.idiomatic: When a broom star or comet transgresses them, executions follow in the inner palace.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches upon them, the rear palace has departures.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses them, women leave the inner palace.

translations.literal: One account says a foreign state presents beautiful women.
translations.idiomatic: One tradition reads this as a foreign power sending beauties as tribute.

sentences.zh: 雲氣化黃，爲後宮有子，喜；

translations.literal: Cloud vapor turning yellow — the rear palace has a child, joy;
translations.idiomatic: Cloud vapor turning yellow means a child born in the inner palace—a cause for celebration;

translations.literal: pale — much illness.
translations.idiomatic: pale vapor foretells widespread illness.

sentences.zh: 尚書五星，在紫微東蕃內，大理東北，《晉志》在東南維，一云在天柱右稍前，主納言，夙夜咨謀，龍作納言之象。

translations.literal: The Imperial Secretariat: five stars, within the eastern rampart of the Purple Forbidden, northeast of the Grand Judge; the Jin Treatise places them at the southeast corner; one account slightly before the Heavenly Pillar on the right; they govern presenting words, consulting day and night — the dragon image of presenting words.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Secretariat comprises five stars within the eastern rampart of the Purple Forbidden, northeast of the Grand Judge. The Jin Treatise locates them at the southeast corner; another tradition places them just before the Heavenly Pillar to the right. They govern the presenting of counsel and deliberation night and day—the celestial image of the dragon who speaks truth to power.

sentences.zh: 彗、孛犯之，官有叛，或太子憂。

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches upon them, officials rebel, or the crown prince is troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses them, officials rebel or the crown prince is in distress.

translations.literal: If a meteor emerges, then the Imperial Secretariat sends envoys;
translations.idiomatic: If a meteor appears to emerge from them, ministers of the Secretariat will be dispatched abroad;

translations.literal: encroaching upon them — remonstrating officials dismissed, the Eight Seats troubled.
translations.idiomatic: a meteor transgressing them means dismissals among remonstrating officials and anxiety among the Eight Seats.

translations.literal: Cloud vapor entering, yellow — joy;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow cloud vapor entering brings celebration;

translations.literal: yellow turning red — the Imperial Secretariat goes to garrison;
translations.idiomatic: yellow turning red means a minister of the Secretariat takes a frontier command;

translations.literal: black — the Imperial Secretariat has those guilty by association.
translations.idiomatic: black portends criminal charges among them.

sentences.zh: 大理二星，在宮門左，一云在尚書前，主平刑斷獄。

translations.literal: The Grand Judge: two stars, left of the palace gate; one account before the Imperial Secretariat; they govern balancing punishments and judging prisons.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Judge comprises two stars to the left of the palace gate—or, by one account, before the Imperial Secretariat. They govern the weighing of punishments and the judgment of cases.

translations.literal: Bright — then penal laws are balanced;
translations.idiomatic: When bright, justice is even-handed;

translations.literal: not bright — then prisons have cruel injustice.
translations.idiomatic: when dim, the prisons fill with cruel wrongs.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon them, noble ministers imprisoned;
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses them, noble ministers are thrown into prison;

translations.literal: color yellow — amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: a yellow hue—amnesty;

translations.literal: white — receive execution;
translations.idiomatic: white—execution;

translations.literal: red-yellow — no guilt;
translations.idiomatic: red-yellow—innocence established;

sentences.zh: 守之，則刑獄冤滯，或刑官有黜。

translations.literal: Stationing itself there — then penal prisons wrongly delayed, or penal officials dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Stationary over them, cases languish unjustly in prison, or penal officials face dismissal.

translations.literal: Comet encroaching — prison officials troubled;
translations.idiomatic: A comet transgressing them troubles the prison officials;

translations.literal: Meteor — the divination is the same.
translations.idiomatic: a meteor—the reading is the same.

translations.literal: Cloud vapor entering, yellow-white — amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow-white cloud vapor entering means amnesty;

translations.literal: Black — judges dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: black portends the dismissal of judges.

sentences.zh: 陰德二星，巫咸圖有之，在尚書西，甘氏云：「陰德外坐在尚書右，陽德外坐在陰德右，太陰太陽入垣翊衛也。

translations.literal: Hidden Virtue: two stars; Wu Xian's chart has them west of the Imperial Secretariat. Master Gan says: 'The Hidden Virtue outer seat is at the Imperial Secretariat's right; the Yang Virtue outer seat is at Hidden Virtue's right — the Moon and Sun enter the rampart as attendant guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Virtue comprises two stars found in Wu Xian's star chart west of the Imperial Secretariat. Master Gan says: 'The outer seat of Hidden Virtue lies to the right of the Imperial Secretariat; the outer seat of Yang Virtue lies to the right of Hidden Virtue—the Moon and Sun enter the rampart as attendant guards.

sentences.zh: 」《天官書》則以「前列直鬥口三星，隨北耑銳，若見若不見，曰陰德。

translations.literal: ' The Treatise on the Celestial Offices says: 'Three stars in the front row, straight at the Dipper mouth, following the north tip sharp, now seen now not seen — called Hidden Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Treatise on the Celestial Offices describes them differently: 'Three stars in the front rank, aligned with the Dipper's mouth, trailing the northern tip to a sharp point—visible one moment, gone the next—called Hidden Virtue.

translations.literal: ' This means bestowing virtue without wishing people to know.
translations.idiomatic: ' This signifies dispensing grace in secret, without desire for recognition.

translations.literal: It governs relieving urgent need and giving comfort.
translations.idiomatic: It governs succor in times of crisis and the comforting of the afflicted.

sentences.zh: 明，則立太子，或女主治天下。

translations.literal: Bright — then establish the crown prince, or the chief consort governs all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When bright, a crown prince will be enthroned—or the chief consort will rule the realm.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon them, drought, famine;
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses them, drought and famine follow;

translations.literal: If it stations itself there, grain is issued to relieve and give aid.
translations.idiomatic: If it stations itself there, grain is distributed to succor the afflicted.

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches, the rear palace harbors treasonous plotting.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses, treason is plotted in the inner palace.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches, the ruler's orders are not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses, the sovereign's commands go unheeded.

translations.literal: Cloud vapor entering, yellow — joy;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow cloud vapor entering portends joy;

translations.literal: bluish-black — sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: bluish-black portends sorrow.

sentences.zh: 天床六星，在紫微垣南門外，主寢舍解息燕休。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Bed: six stars, outside the south gate of the Purple Forbidden Enclosure, governing sleeping quarters, rest, repose, and easeful leisure.
translations.idiomatic: The six stars of the Heavenly Bed lie beyond the south gate of the Purple Forbidden Enclosure; they govern chambers of rest, respite, and the sovereign's easeful repose.

sentences.zh: 一曰在二樞之間，備幸之所也。

translations.literal: One account says they lie between the Two Pivots — the place kept ready for imperial visits.
translations.idiomatic: Some place them between the Two Pivots—the lodging prepared for the emperor's visits.

sentences.zh: 陶隱居云：「傾則天王失位。

translations.literal: Tao Hongjing writes: 'If it tilts, the Celestial King loses his throne.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Hongjing observes: 'When it tilts, the Heavenly Sovereign is displaced.

sentences.zh: 」客星入宮中，有刺客，或內侍憂。

translations.literal: ' When a guest star enters the palace, there are assassins, or anxiety among inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: ' When a guest star enters the palace, assassins appear—or the eunuch attendants are gripped with fear.

sentences.zh: 彗、孛犯之，主憂，大臣失位。

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches them, the sovereign is troubled, and great ministers lose their posts.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses them, the ruler falls into distress and high ministers are dismissed.

sentences.zh: 流星犯，后妃叛，女主立，或人君易位。

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches, empresses and consorts rebel, a female ruler is enthroned, or the sovereign is replaced.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses, consorts revolt, a woman takes the throne, or the ruler is overthrown.

sentences.zh: 雲氣入，色黃，天子得美女，後宮喜有子；

translations.literal: Cloud vapor entering, color yellow — the Son of Heaven obtains a beautiful woman, and the inner palace rejoices at bearing a son;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow cloud vapor entering means the Son of Heaven gains a fair consort, and the inner palace celebrates the birth of an heir;

translations.literal: pale blue-white — the sovereign is unsettled; bluish-black — sorrow;
translations.idiomatic: pale blue-white—the sovereign's peace is disturbed; bluish-black—grief;

translations.literal: white — ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: white bodes ill.

sentences.zh: 華蓋七星，杠九星，如蓋有柄下垂，以覆大帝之坐也，在紫微宮臨勾陳之上。

translations.literal: The Canopy: seven stars; the Pole: nine stars — like a canopy with a handle hanging down, to cover the Great Thearch's seat; in the Purple Forbidden Palace, overlooking the Hook Array above.
translations.idiomatic: The Canopy comprises seven stars; the Pole, nine—shaped like a canopy with a pendant handle, spread above the Great Thearch's throne. It stands within the Purple Forbidden Palace, poised over the Hook Array.

translations.literal: Upright — auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: When upright—auspicious;

translations.literal: if tilted — then ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: if tilted—calamity follows.

sentences.zh: 客星犯之，王室有憂，兵起。

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches it, the royal house has cause for worry, and war arises.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses it, the royal house is troubled and war breaks out.

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches, war arises and the state changes its government.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses, war erupts and the realm changes hands.

sentences.zh: 流星犯，兵起宮內，以赦解之；

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches, war arises within the palace — resolved by amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses, strife rises within the palace, but a general amnesty may lift the curse;

translations.literal: Piercing through the Canopy — calamity for the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: A star streaking through the Canopy portends disaster for the Three Excellencies.

translations.literal: Cloud vapor entering, yellow-white — the sovereign rejoices;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow-white cloud vapor entering brings joy to the ruler;

translations.literal: red-yellow — marquises and kings rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: red-yellow brings gladness to the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 傳舍九星，在華蓋上，近河，賓客之館，主北使入中國。

translations.literal: The Relay Inn: nine stars, upon the Canopy, near the River — a lodging for guests; it governs northern envoys entering China.
translations.idiomatic: The nine stars of the Relay Inn rest upon the Canopy, close to the River—a celestial guesthouse governing emissaries from the north entering the Middle Kingdom.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches, the state has cause for worry;
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses, the realm is troubled;

translations.literal: One account says: when a guest star stations itself there, guard against treacherous envoys;
translations.idiomatic: Some say that when a guest star stations itself there, one must beware of deceitful emissaries;

translations.literal: it also signifies that war arises in the northern lands.
translations.idiomatic: others read it as war stirring on the northern frontier.

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches and stations there, it likewise signifies northern troops.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses and stations there, northern armies are likewise foretold.

translations.literal: Black cloud vapor entering — northern troops invade China.
translations.idiomatic: Black cloud vapor entering foretells northern armies marching upon the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 八穀八星，在華蓋西、五車北，一曰在諸王西。

translations.literal: The Eight Grains: eight stars, west of the Canopy and north of the Five Chariots; one account places them west of the Various Lords.
translations.idiomatic: The eight stars of the Eight Grains lie west of the Canopy and north of the Five Chariots; some place them west of the Various Lords.

sentences.zh: 武密曰：「主候歲豐儉，一稻、二黍、三大麥、四小麥、五大豆、六小豆、七粟、八麻。

translations.literal: Wu Mi says: 'They govern watching the year's abundance and scarcity: first rice, second millet, third great wheat, fourth small wheat, fifth great beans, sixth small beans, seventh hulled grain, eighth hemp.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mi writes: 'They oversee the year's harvest—whether bounty or want: first rice, second millet, third barley, fourth wheat, fifth soybeans, sixth mung beans, seventh grain, eighth hemp.

sentences.zh: 」甘氏曰：「八谷在宮北門之右，司親耕，司候歲，司尚食。

translations.literal: ' Master Gan says: 'The Eight Grains lie to the right of the palace's north gate; they oversee the emperor's plowing, oversee the year's harvest, and oversee the imperial kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: ' Master Gan adds: 'The Eight Grains stand to the right of the palace's north gate, charged with the sovereign's first furrow, the watching of the harvest, and the provisioning of the imperial table.

translations.literal: ' The stars bright — auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: ' When the stars shine bright—auspicious;

translations.literal: one star lost — one grain fails to ripen;
translations.idiomatic: one star vanishes—one crop fails;

translations.literal: all eight stars invisible — great famine.
translations.idiomatic: all eight stars disappear—famine stalks the land.

translations.literal: When a guest star enters, grain grows costly.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star enters, grain prices soar.

translations.literal: When a comet enters, it becomes flood.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet enters, floodwaters rise.

translations.literal: When black cloud vapor encroaches them, the eight grains are not harvested.
translations.idiomatic: When black cloud vapor transgresses them, none of the eight grains can be gathered in.

sentences.zh: 內階六星，在文昌東北，天皇之階也。

translations.literal: The Inner Steps: six stars, northeast of Literary Glory — the Heavenly Sovereign's staircase.
translations.idiomatic: The six stars of the Inner Steps lie northeast of Literary Glory—the celestial staircase of the Heavenly Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 一曰上帝幸文館之內階也。

translations.literal: One account says they are the inner steps of the Literary Hall where the Supreme Lord visits.
translations.idiomatic: Some identify them as the inner staircase of the Literary Hall, where the Supreme Lord holds audience.

translations.literal: Bright — auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: When bright—auspicious;

translations.literal: tilting and trembling — worry.
translations.idiomatic: when they tilt and tremble—anxiety follows.

sentences.zh: 彗、孛、客、流星犯之，人君遜避之象。

translations.literal: When a comet, broom star, guest star, or shooting star encroaches them, it is the image of the ruler yielding and withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet, broom star, guest star, or meteor transgresses them, it presages the ruler's abdication or retreat.

sentences.zh: 文昌六星，在北斗魁前、紫微垣西，天之六府也，主集計天道。

translations.literal: Literary Glory: six stars, before the Northern Dipper's bowl and west of the Purple Forbidden Enclosure — Heaven's six treasuries; they govern gathering and reckoning the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The six stars of Literary Glory stand before the Dipper's bowl, west of the Purple Forbidden Enclosure—Heaven's six ministries, charged with tallying the courses of the celestial Way.

sentences.zh: 一曰上將、大將軍，建威武；

translations.literal: The first is called the Grand General and Great General — establishing martial awesomeness;
translations.idiomatic: The first corresponds to the Grand General and Commander-in-Chief—establishing martial majesty;

translations.literal: the second, the Deputy General and Master of Writing — rectifying left and right;
translations.idiomatic: the second to the Lieutenant General and Master of Writing—keeping the court in order;

translations.literal: the third, the Noble Minister and Grand Steward — managing the threads of literature;
translations.idiomatic: the third to the Noble Counselor and Grand Steward—overseeing the realm's literary affairs;

sentences.zh: 四曰司祿、司中、司隸，賞功進；

translations.literal: the fourth, the Director of Emolument, Director of the Center, and Director of Corrections — rewarding merit and advancing the worthy;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth to the Directors of Salary, of the Center, and of Penal Supervision—rewarding merit and advancing the deserving;

sentences.zh: 五曰司命、司怪、太史，主滅咎；

translations.literal: the fifth, the Director of Fate, Director of Prodigies, and Grand Historian — governing the quelling of calamities;
translations.idiomatic: the fifth to the Directors of Fate and of Prodigies, and the Grand Historian—charged with warding off misfortune;

translations.literal: the sixth, the Director of Bandits and Grand Judge — assisting in governing the state's treasures and law.
translations.idiomatic: the sixth to the Director of Criminal Matters and the Grand Judge—assisting in the administration of justice and the royal treasury.

sentences.zh: 所謂一者，起北斗魁前近內階者也。

translations.literal: The so-called first begins from before the Northern Dipper's bowl, near the Inner Steps.
translations.idiomatic: The first of these begins before the Dipper's bowl, close by the Inner Steps.

sentences.zh: 明潤色黃，大小齊，天瑞臻，四海安；

translations.literal: Bright, moist, and yellow in color, uniform in size — heavenly auspices arrive, and the four seas are at peace;
translations.idiomatic: When they shine bright and golden, evenly matched in magnitude, heavenly blessings descend and all under Heaven knows peace;

translations.literal: bluish-black, faint and fine — then much slaughter and harm;
translations.idiomatic: when they turn bluish-black and dim, bloodshed multiplies;

translations.literal: when they tremble — the Three Excellencies are dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: when they quake—the Three Excellencies fall from power.

translations.literal: When the Moon halos their lodge — great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: When the Moon halos their asterism, a general amnesty is proclaimed.

translations.literal: When the Year Star stations itself there, war arises.
translations.idiomatic: When the Year Star stations itself there, war breaks out.

translations.literal: When the Sparkling Deluder stations itself there, generals meet ill fortune.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sparkling Deluder stations itself there, disaster befalls the generals.

translations.literal: When the Great White stations itself there or enters — war rises.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great White stations itself there or enters, war flares up.

translations.literal: When the Stationary Star stations itself there, the state is secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the Stationary Star stations itself there, the realm enjoys stability.

translations.literal: When a guest star stations itself there, great ministers rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star stations itself there, high ministers turn traitor.

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches, great chaos.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses, the realm is plunged into chaos.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches, chaos within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses, turmoil erupts within the palace.

sentences.zh: 三公三星，在北斗杓南及魁第一星西，一云在斗柄東，爲太尉、司徒、司空之象。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies: three stars, south of the Northern Dipper's ladle and west of the bowl's first star; one account places them east of the dipper handle — images of the Grand Commandant, Minister over the Masses, and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The three stars of the Three Excellencies lie south of the Dipper's ladle and west of its leading star; some place them east of the handle—they embody the Grand Commandant, the Minister over the Masses, and the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 在魁西者名三師，占與三公同，皆主宣德化、調七政、和陰陽之官也。

translations.literal: Those west of the bowl are called the Three Preceptors; their omens are the same as the Three Excellencies — all officials who govern spreading virtue and teaching, adjusting the seven governances, and harmonizing yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: Those west of the bowl are named the Three Preceptors; their portents match the Three Excellencies—all signs of officers charged with disseminating virtue, regulating the seven powers, and harmonizing yin and yang.

translations.literal: Shifting position — inauspicious;
translations.idiomatic: When they shift from their places—ill fortune;

translations.literal: remaining in their usual positions — then peace.
translations.idiomatic: when they hold their accustomed stations—all is well.

translations.literal: One star lost — the realm is in peril;
translations.idiomatic: One star vanishes—the realm teeters on the brink;

translations.literal: two stars lost — the realm falls into chaos;
translations.idiomatic: two vanish—chaos spreads across the land;

translations.literal: all three stars invisible — the realm goes ungoverned.
translations.idiomatic: all three disappear—the realm knows no governance.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches, the Three Excellencies are troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses, the Three Excellencies are beset with worry.

sentences.zh: 彗、孛及流星犯之，三公死。

translations.literal: When a comet, broom star, or meteor encroaches them, the Three Excellencies die.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet, broom star, or meteor transgresses them, the Three Excellencies perish.

sentences.zh: 天牢六星，在北斗魁下，貴人之牢也，主繩愆禁暴。

translations.literal: The Heavenly Prison: six stars, beneath the Northern Dipper's bowl — a prison for the noble; it governs binding faults and restraining violence.
translations.idiomatic: The six stars of the Heavenly Prison hang beneath the Dipper's bowl—a celestial jail for the exalted, charged with punishing transgression and curbing brutality.

translations.literal: Master Gan says: 'A prison for the lowly.
translations.idiomatic: Master Gan reads them differently: 'A prison for the common people.

translations.literal: ' When the Moon's halo enters — many thieves.
translations.idiomatic: ' When the Moon's halo crosses them, theft proliferates.

sentences.zh: 熒惑犯之，民相食，國有敗兵。

translations.literal: When the Sparkling Deluder encroaches them, the people eat one another, and the state has defeated troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sparkling Deluder transgresses them, men devour one another and the armies are routed.

translations.literal: When the Great White and Year Star station themselves there, the state has many violations of law.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great White and Year Star station themselves there, lawlessness spreads through the realm.

sentences.zh: 客星、彗星犯之，三公下獄，或將相憂。

translations.literal: When a guest star or comet encroaches them, the Three Excellencies are cast into prison, or generals and ministers are troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star or comet transgresses them, the Three Excellencies are imprisoned—or generals and ministers fall into despair.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches them, there is a decree of amnesty and pardon.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses them, an edict of clemency is issued.

sentences.zh: 勢四星，在太陽守西北，一曰在璣星北。

translations.literal: Power: four stars, northwest of the Sun Guardian; one account places them north of the Ji Star.
translations.idiomatic: The four stars of Power lie northwest of the Sun Guardian; some place them north of the Ji Star.

sentences.zh: 勢，腐形人也，主助宣王命，內常侍官也。

translations.literal: Power — deformed persons; it governs assisting in proclaiming the king's commands — officials of the inner palace attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Power signifies those of corrupted form—eunuchs who assist in promulgating the royal will, the officers of the inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 以不明爲吉，明則閹人擅權。

translations.literal: Taking dimness as auspicious; if bright, eunuchs monopolize power.
translations.idiomatic: Dimness is counted auspicious; brightness means eunuchs seize the reins of power.

sentences.zh: 天理四星，在北斗魁中，貴人之牢也。

translations.literal: Heavenly Principle: four stars, within the Northern Dipper's bowl — a prison for the noble.
translations.idiomatic: The four stars of Heavenly Principle rest within the Dipper's bowl—a celestial prison for the highborn.

sentences.zh: 星不欲明，其中有星則貴人下獄。

translations.literal: The stars should not be bright; if a star appears within them, nobles are cast into prison.
translations.idiomatic: These stars ought not shine brightly; should a star glimmer within them, the nobility fills the dungeons.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches, there are many prisons.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses, the prisons overflow.

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches them, the state is in peril.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses them, the realm faces ruin.

sentences.zh: 赤雲氣犯之，兵大起，將相行兵。

translations.literal: When red cloud vapor encroaches them, war rises greatly, and generals and ministers take the field.
translations.idiomatic: When red cloud vapor transgresses them, war engulfs the land and generals and ministers march to battle.

sentences.zh: 相一星，在北斗第四星南，總百司，集衆事，掌邦典，以佐帝王。

translations.literal: The Minister Star: one star, south of the Northern Dipper's fourth star — overseeing the hundred offices, gathering all affairs, holding the state's statutes, to assist the emperor and king.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister Star, a solitary star south of the Dipper's fourth, oversees the hundred bureaus, gathers every matter of state, and holds the kingdom's laws—in service to the throne.

sentences.zh: 一曰在中鬥文昌之南，在朝少師行大宰者。

translations.literal: One account places it south of the Central Dipper's Literary Glory — in court, the Junior Preceptor acting as Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Some locate it south of Literary Glory in the Central Dipper—the celestial counterpart of the Junior Preceptor serving as Grand Steward.

translations.literal: Bright — auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: When bright—auspicious;

translations.literal: dim — ill omen;
translations.idiomatic: when dim—ill fortune;

translations.literal: lost — then the minister is dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: when it vanishes—the chief minister is removed.

sentences.zh: 太陽守一星，在相星西北、鬥第三星西南，大將、大臣之象，主設武備以戒不虞。

translations.literal: The Sun Guardian: one star, northwest of the Minister Star and southwest of the Dipper's third star — the image of a great general and great minister; it governs setting martial preparations to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: The Sun Guardian, a single star northwest of the Minister Star and southwest of the Dipper's third, embodies the great general and minister—it presides over martial readiness against unforeseen peril.

sentences.zh: 一曰在下臺北，太尉官也，在朝少傅行大司馬者。

translations.literal: One account places it north of the Lower Terrace — the office of Grand Commandant; in court, the Junior Tutor acting as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Some place it north of the Lower Terrace—the seat of the Grand Commandant, the Junior Tutor wielding the authority of Grand Marshal.

translations.literal: Bright — auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: When bright—auspicious;

translations.literal: dim — ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: when dim—calamity.

sentences.zh: 客、彗、孛犯之，爲易政，將相憂，兵亂。

translations.literal: When a guest star, comet, or broom star encroaches it, the government changes, generals and ministers are troubled, and military chaos ensues.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star, comet, or broom star transgresses it, the regime is overturned, generals and ministers are imperiled, and armies clash in confusion.

translations.literal: Cloud vapor entering, yellow — joy;
translations.idiomatic: Yellow cloud vapor entering portends rejoicing;

translations.literal: pale blue-white — the general dies;
translations.idiomatic: pale blue-white—a general's death;

translations.literal: red — great ministers are troubled.
translations.idiomatic: red—ministers consumed with dread.

sentences.zh: 內廚二星，在紫微垣西南外，主六宮之內飲食及后妃夫人與太子燕飲。

translations.literal: The Inner Kitchen: two stars, outside the southwest of the Purple Forbidden Enclosure; they govern food and drink within the six palaces, and the convivial feasting of empresses, consorts, ladies, and the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The two stars of the Inner Kitchen stand beyond the southwest of the Purple Forbidden Enclosure; they govern the victuals of the six inner palaces and the banquet companionship of empresses, consorts, noble ladies, and the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 彗、孛或流星犯之，飲食有毒。

translations.literal: Comet, broom star, or meteor encroaching upon them — food and drink are poisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet, broom star, or meteor transgresses them, food and drink turn poisonous.

sentences.zh: 天廚六星，在扶筐北，一曰在東北維外，主盛饌，今光祿廚也。

translations.literal: Celestial Kitchen: six stars, north of the Holding Basket; one account places them outside the northeast corner. They govern lavish banquets — the modern Director of Imperial Commissary.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Kitchen comprises six stars north of the Holding Basket—or, by one account, outside the northeast corner. They govern lavish banquets and represent the Director of Imperial Commissary.

translations.literal: When the stars vanish, famine;
translations.idiomatic: When the stars vanish, famine follows;

translations.literal: when they cannot be seen, disaster.
translations.idiomatic: when they cannot be seen, calamity follows.

translations.literal: When a guest star or meteor encroaches upon them, famine also.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star or meteor transgresses them, famine also follows.

sentences.zh: 天一一星，在紫微宮門右星南，天帝之神也，主戰鬥，知吉凶。

translations.literal: Celestial One: a single star, south of the star at the right gate of the Purple Palace — the numen of the Celestial Thearch. It governs warfare and discerns fortune from calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Celestial One is a single star south of the star at the right gate of the Purple Palace—the numen of the Celestial Thearch. It governs warfare and discerns fortune from calamity.

sentences.zh: 明，則陰陽和，萬物盛，人君吉；

translations.literal: When bright, yin and yang are harmonious, all things flourish, and the ruler is blessed;
translations.idiomatic: When bright, yin and yang fall into harmony, all things flourish, and the ruler is blessed;

translations.literal: when it vanishes, the realm falls into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: when it vanishes, the realm falls into chaos.

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon it, the five grains grow costly.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest star transgresses it, the five grains grow costly.

translations.literal: When a comet or broom star encroaches upon it, ministers rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When a comet or broom star transgresses it, ministers rebel.

translations.literal: When a meteor encroaches upon it, war arises and the people take flight.
translations.idiomatic: When a meteor transgresses it, war arises and the people take flight.

translations.literal: When cloud vapor encroaches upon it in yellow, ruler and ministers are in harmony;
translations.idiomatic: When yellow cloud vapor transgresses it, ruler and ministers are in harmony;

translations.literal: in black, the chancellor is dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: in black, the chancellor is dismissed.

sentences.zh: 太一一星，在天一南相近一度，亦天帝神也，主使十六神，知風雨、水旱、兵革、饑饉、疾疫、災害所在之國也。

translations.literal: Grand One: a single star about one degree south of Celestial One, close by — also a numen of the Celestial Thearch. It commands the sixteen spirits and discerns where wind and rain, flood and drought, war, famine, pestilence, and disaster will fall upon which kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Grand One is a single star about one degree south of Celestial One, close by—also a numen of the Celestial Thearch. It commands the sixteen spirits and discerns where wind and rain, flood and drought, war, famine, pestilence, and disaster will strike which kingdom.

translations.literal: When bright, auspicious;
translations.idiomatic: When bright, the omen is auspicious;

translations.literal: when dim, calamity;
translations.idiomatic: when dim, calamity follows;

translations.literal: when displaced from its position, flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: when displaced from its position, flood and drought follow.

sentences.zh: 客星犯，兵起，民流，火災，水旱，饑饉。

translations.literal: When a guest star encroaches upon it, war arises, the people flee, fires break out, flood and drought afflict the land, and famine follows.
